decision: Retain the physical ferry-state repair on this draft. The paired score improved at both widths and remains below 9.5. Retrieval promotion is a separate measurement.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show the path, ferry, and footbridge closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus and selection; all three closures appeared.

A-1440.edge_observation: ArrowRight wrapped from 6 m to 2 m; only the riverside path closure remained.
A-1440.fact_check: The water surface aligns with the 6 m line, and the ferry is shown at the surface with a Stopped label. Actual local thresholds and live conditions are unsupported by the view.
A-1440.strength: The cross-section, threshold lines, and closure list make the consequence of the selection easy to compare.
A-1440.weakness: The illustration occupies much more space than the actionable closure list, and the graphic has no explicit indication that it is illustrative rather than live data.
A-1440.repair: Add a concise data source and update time, or clearly label the display as an illustrative scenario.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures within the first viewport.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus and selection; the complete three-item list and cross-section fit within the 390 × 844 viewport.

A-390.edge_observation: ArrowRight wrapped to 2 m, leaving only the riverside path closure.
A-390.fact_check: The water surface aligns with 6 m and the ferry sits at the surface; Stopped reinforces the list. Real crossing conditions and thresholds are unsupported by the view.
A-390.strength: The controls, complete result, and diagram are readable together without scrolling at the tested viewport.
A-390.weakness: The small illustration makes the ferry and path details less distinct, and the source of the closure thresholds is absent.
A-390.repair: Keep the compact layout but add a concise source or scenario label and preserve legible diagram details.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show the path, ferry, and footbridge closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus and selection; all three closures appeared.

B-1440.edge_observation: ArrowRight wrapped to 2 m; only the riverside path closure remained.
B-1440.fact_check: The water surface aligns with the 6 m line, but the ferry remains at the 4 m line visibly underwater while the text says it stops. Actual local thresholds and live conditions are unsupported by the view.
B-1440.strength: The threshold diagram and concise list give the selected level a clear visual hierarchy.
B-1440.weakness: The submerged ferry conflicts with the depicted water surface and makes the illustration harder to trust.
B-1440.repair: Move the ferry with the water surface and show its stopped status explicitly.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures within the first viewport.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus and selection; the complete list and cross-section fit within the 390 × 844 viewport.

B-390.edge_observation: ArrowRight wrapped to 2 m, leaving only the riverside path closure.
B-390.fact_check: The water surface reaches 6 m, but the ferry remains at 4 m beneath it. Real crossing conditions and thresholds are unsupported by the view.
B-390.strength: The full result is visible at once, with clear controls and a visible keyboard focus indicator.
B-390.weakness: The small submerged ferry gives a misleading physical picture and has no stopped indicator in the diagram.
B-390.repair: Place the ferry at the selected water surface, add a stopped label, and identify the source or illustrative nature of the thresholds.

preference.reason: Both versions support the keyboard task and fit the complete result in the tested mobile viewport. A also places the ferry at the selected water surface and labels it stopped, while B leaves it underwater at 6 m.
